item.content:encoded:
Votes don't help the author, so I've vowed to always leave a comment with mine, at the very least whenever I rate an article negatively. If you feel the same, help out by leaving critique with more of your votes. Comment follows:

The format here is terrible. The green and red conflict horribly. Even the black and purple at the bottom - though I'm unsure if other formats in the canon also use the same style - evokes feelings of "my first gradient". The styling is clearly taken from the Thorn Valley article, with not enough changes to make it not look like a ripoff - the borders, the font, the image positioning the reviews - but enough poor changes to nosedive it.

Part of the fun of Ambrose, for me, is the theming. I can excuse the clownish colours, just, but it's just not different enough from Thorn Valley. It's a -1 from me but if you update the CSS to make it different, please let me know and I'll be happy to judge it on its own merits.

item.content:encoded: Author, for future reference, if you make a goi format for a goi without a tag, you tag it with "_other".

I heard about it from my foreign student friend. I knew it was a little ways off but seeing him get fat got me curious. And man, was it the best place for seafood! In the mountains! They were very generous and made me a custom Siren and Shrimp Sisig without a reservation. I got some Mead to drink and it went down so smooth, I became diabetic and jaundiced at the same time. Worth it! I gotta ask though if the fish scales come off, it's been spreading. Still worth it!

item.title: New Branch
item.content:encoded:
First of all, a big big thanks to Proasek for his guidance and approval on the new branch. The style is a modified version of Amber Thorn Valley by mayoculpa. It's an ironed banana leaf version of the Ambrose format.

Now unto the food. As you may have noticed, its all monsters or sacred beasts from local mythology. The way it's served however is reminiscent of Filipino cuisine and culture. Filipinos love buffets, eating in a group, and dishing out a copious amount of it on ironed banana leaves. There is a lot of meat (seafood counts as meat), and the cooking styles can be interchanged with each meat. Filipinos are heavy meat eaters, hardly any vegans, and some of the leading causes of mortality are hypertensive stroke, heart disease, diabetes and colon cancer, and I tried to reflect all of that in the piece.

Some of other elements also come from Filipino Mythology, such as reversing your shirt when lost and Maria Makiling's mountain. The Mountain and University exists in reality, but it's one of the more anomalous tourist spots in the Philippines.

I hope you enjoy it. Thanks. P.S. There's a secret menu.

Misty Forest picture is from:
https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Mud_Spring,_Mount_Makiling_-_panoramio.jpg

The two Baybayin texts were generated using this and made into transparent background images by me.

"Mabuhay" - common Tagalog greeting meaning "Live Prosperously"


"Paalam at Salamat" - translated as "Farewell and Thanks"
